RESONANT CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING
OBJECTIVES
w Identify an open component in a resonant circuit.
w Identify a shorted component in a resonant circuit.
w Identify a changed value component in a resonant circuit.
w Observe the effects of an open component in a series and parallel resonant circuit.
w Observe the effects of a shorted component in a series
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Definition
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 20A
In this lesson, you will learn about troubleshooting series and parallel resonant circuits.
INTRODUCTIONM
Troubleshooting a resonant circuit requires identifying the circuit as faulty and then isolating the fault to the failed component........
Voltage measurements across the circuit's resistor can quickly determine if the circuit is operating correctly.
Resistance measurements isolate and verify the fault to one of the three components.
Let's begin the lesson on RESONANT CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING..................
LESSON MENU
RESONANT CIRCUIT FAULTS
DISCUSSION
The three most common faults in a resonant circuit are the same as in other LCR circuits. A resonant circuit is an LCR circuit.
However, due to the characteristics of resonance, the troubleshooting techniques are simpler. You do not have to calculate individual component voltage drops.
Calculating the resonant frequency is all that is required.
The effects on the circuit of an open, short, or changed value component depend on whether the components are in series or in parallel...
Let's discuss series resonant circuit faults first.
This series circuit produces a voltage drop across R based on the frequency of the applied voltage.

In a series circuit, Er is maximum at the resonant frequency. This means that if we find the point at which Er is maximum, then the frequency that we measure at that point is the resonant frequency...
Comparing the calculated resonant frequency with the measured frequency, checks for normal operation..r normal operation.
Observing that Er decreases as the frequency deviates from the resonant frequency checks for normal operation....................
If one of the components opens, current flow in the series circuit stops.
Voltage measurements quickly identify which component is open.
The open component measures the applied voltage and the other components measure 0 V.
Recall that in theory, ignoring the voltage drop across the inductor due to its' coil resistance, Er measures the applied voltage at resonance.
However, the inductor and capacitor do not measure 0V if the circuit is operating correctly.o
Resistance measurements are made to verify that the component is open.
Remember that in a series circuit, an open stops current flow and the open component measures the applied voltage.
If one of the reactive components (L or C) shorts, the circuit no longer behaves like an LCR circuit. It effectively becomes either RL or RC, and resonance is no longer a factor..

The voltage across the resistor will not decrease as the frequency increases above resonance if the inductor is shorted. stead, the voltage will act as it does in an RC circuit. It will start at minimum, at lower frequencies, and will increase to a maximum as frequency increases.

Voltage measurements quickly determine which reactive component is shorted.
The shorted component measures 0V and the other components measure some voltage value.
If the resistor shorts, its voltage drop measures 0V. The circuit still has a resonant frequency, but you cannot measure for maximum Er at resonance.
Resistance measurements are made to verify that the component is shorted. The inductor should measure some small value of resistance.
Remember that in a series circuit, a shorted component measures 0V and the other components measure some value of voltage.
If one of the reactive components (L or C) changes value, the resonant frequency changes..
Er will not be maximum at the correct frequency..
To determine which reactive component has changed value, you must use a capacitor or inductor bridge tester.
If the tester is not available, replace C and L one at a time until the circuit is operating normally.
If the resistor changes value, you will see little effect. Er is maximum at resonance no matter what the value of R is..
In this case, a simple resistance measurement across R verifies whether or not the resistor has changed value.
Remember, a changed value component changes circuit values. There is no indication of an open or short.

Now, let's discuss faults in a parallel resonant circuit...
This parallel circuit produces a voltage drop across the sampling resistor based on the frequency of the applied voltage.
In this circuit, Ers is minimum at the resonant frequency.uency.
With Ers at minimum, comparing the measured frequency with the calculated resonant frequency checks for normal operation...............................
Observing the fact that Ers increases as the frequency deviates from the resonant frequency provides another check for normal operation.
If one of the reactive components (L or C) opens, the circuit is no longer an LCR circuit and resonance is no longer a factor.
The voltage drop across the sampling resistor does not fall to a minimum at resonance as we would expect from a parallel LCR circuit.
An open capacitor produces an RL circuit. Ers decreases when frequency increases because XL increases.
An open inductor produces an RC circuit. Ers increases when frequency increases because Xc decreases.
Breaking the circuit and making current measurements verifies the open reactive component.
Current does not flow through an open component. The branch that has the open measures 0 A current.
